## Beat 0 — Gas occupies real space

> Thin gas fills the space between a distant quasar and us — denser in filaments, emptier in voids.
The quasar's light crosses it along one line. What does the gas along that line do to the light?

- **Learning objective.** There is real gas distributed through a volume, and our light samples one path through it.
- **User action.** Move along the beam (hover near it, or press and slide along it); drag the gas to turn the volume. The cross-section, the stretch of the strip and the density reading report where you are.
- **Visible physical consequence.** The probe follows the hand along the beam; the cut through the volume, the cross-section around the beam, the highlighted stretch of the strip and the density reading follow it. Turned, the volume shows parallax — the beam passes behind near gas and in front of far gas.
- **Optional equations ("show the physics").**
  - $ \bar n_{\rm H}(z{=}3) \approx 1.2\times10^{-5}\ {\rm cm^{-3}} $ — about a dozen hydrogen nuclei per cubic metre, on average (SCI-CTX-001)
- **Linked provenance.** SCI-REP-002 (The 3D slab is a teaching volume; only gas on the beam absorbs; verified), SCI-SIM-TOY-001 (The toy Zel'dovich volume used by the canonical prototype; verified), SCI-CTX-001 (Mean hydrogen density of the universe at z = 3; verified), SCI-CTX-005 (Velocity scales along the sightline; verified-numeric), SCI-RED-004 (Comoving distance along the light's path (Planck 2018); verified)
- **Validation.** VAL-TOY-001: pass
- **Deliberate simplifications.** The observer and the quasar are drawn at the ends of the beam for orientation only; the beam is broken at each end because the gaps are not to scale — the toy sample lies ≈ 4384 Mpc/h (comoving) from us, and the quasar farther still (SCI-RED-004). The volume is a 20 × 8 × 8 Mpc/h teaching block from a Zel'dovich toy field, not a hydrodynamic simulation (SCI-SIM-TOY-001). Gas near the beam is drawn darker; that emphasis is ours (focus rule, SCI-REP-002). Perspective and the single slow drift on entry are display depth cues. The drawing dissolves into paper toward the sample's edges — the sample ends, the gas does not; "show the physics" draws the sample's boundary (SCI-REP-002).
- **Visual transformations.**
  - VT-GAS-DEPTH: the gas volume in shallow depth — near gas in front of the beam, far gas behind it, paler with distance; its edges dissolve into paper — the toy volume's density around the beam (a 20 × 8 × 8 Mpc/h sample) → ink in depth (stacked translucent slices) (SCI-REP-002, SCI-SIM-TOY-001)

## Beat 1 — Same gas, different scale

> Zoom into one parcel on the beam: the smooth gas is a crowd of protons, helium nuclei and electrons — atoms with their electrons knocked off by ultraviolet light from galaxies and quasars.
About one hydrogen atom in 100 000 is still neutral (a few times more in a filament) — and only those can absorb the light.

- **Learning objective.** A macroscopic gas parcel is a vast microscopic population, almost all ionised; the atoms drawn next are a representative few.
- **User action.** Set the magnification (an instrument setting) from the volume, to one parcel, to its particles, to the neutral atoms.
- **Visible physical consequence.** Nested frames show the same gas at four scales; the stipple of ionised particles gives way to the rare neutral atoms, which are then gathered for display.
- **Progressive reveal.** volume (the gas fills the volume; the beam crosses it) → one parcel (still smooth gas, 1 Mpc/h across) → particles (protons and electrons; a rare neutral atom) → neutral atoms (representative atoms · not to scale)
- **Optional equations ("show the physics").**
  - $ N_{\rm H}\ \text{in a 100 kpc parcel} \sim 10^{66} $ — a 100 kpc (proper) parcel at about 5× the mean density — smaller than the 1 Mpc/h frame drawn; only about one in 10⁵ of these nuclei carries its electron (a neutral atom), the rest are protons and free electrons (SCI-CTX-007, SCI-ION-002)
- **Linked provenance.** SCI-REP-001 (Representative atoms are a cartoon sample; verified), SCI-REP-006 (Four representations of the same gas, never mixed silently; verified), SCI-CTX-001 (Mean hydrogen density of the universe at z = 3; verified), SCI-CTX-004 (H I photoionisation rate at z ≈ 3; verified), SCI-CTX-007 (Parcel sizes and atom counts; verified), SCI-ION-001 (Photoionisation equilibrium and the neutral-amount control; verified), SCI-ION-002 (How neutral the IGM is; verified), SCI-RED-004 (Comoving distance along the light's path (Planck 2018); verified)
- **Validation.** VAL-TOY-001: pass
- **Deliberate simplifications.** The observer and the quasar are drawn at the ends of the beam for orientation only; the beam is broken at each end because the gaps are not to scale — the toy sample lies ≈ 4384 Mpc/h (comoving) from us, and the quasar farther still (SCI-RED-004). The atoms are a representative sample (a few hundred), not a count and not simulation particles (SCI-REP-001). The particle stage shows the ionised majority as a stipple, with neutral atoms drawn far more common than the true 1 in ~10⁵; from Beat 2 on only neutral atoms are drawn (SCI-ION-002, SCI-REP-006). Atom motions are straight lines (collisions are rare at these densities) and slowed enormously for display.

## Beat 2 — One atom meets one colour

> Among these colours of the quasar's light, hydrogen responds to one: Lyman-alpha, 1215.67 Å — ultraviolet — in the atom's own frame. (Its weaker siblings, such as Lyman-β, return in Beat 13.)
A moving atom sees colours Doppler-shifted, so a different colour comes into resonance — and is scattered out of the beam.

- **Learning objective.** The physical origin of the shadow is resonant scattering of one colour in the atom's frame.
- **User action.** Push the atom along the beam (drag its motion); the speed ruler reports it; switch to "one colour, many atoms".
- **Visible physical consequence.** A different photon colour is caught and scattered sideways out of the beam; the atom-frame panel shows which colour sits on the resonance.
- **Optional equations ("show the physics").**
  - $ \lambda_{\rm res} = \lambda_0\,\Bigl(1 + \dfrac{v}{c}\Bigr),\quad \lambda_0 = 1215.67\ \text{Å} $ — an atom moving away from us (v > 0) brings a redder colour into resonance (SCI-ATOM-001, SCI-ATOM-002, SCI-MAP-003)
  - $ \text{1s} \to \text{2p} \to \text{1s} + \gamma\ (\text{random direction}),\ \ t_{\rm 2p} \approx 1.6\ {\rm ns} $ — the photon is re-emitted, but almost never back into our narrow beam — so it is lost to us (SCI-RES-001)
- **Linked provenance.** SCI-ATOM-001 (Lyα (H I 1s → 2p) transition data; verified), SCI-ATOM-002 (Resonance in the atom's frame (Doppler condition); verified), SCI-RES-001 (Lyα "absorption" in the IGM is resonant scattering out of the beam; verified), SCI-MAP-003 (Peculiar-velocity sign convention; verified), SCI-REP-004 (Natural width is magnified wherever it is drawn; verified)
- **Validation.** VAL-MAP-001: pass
- **Deliberate simplifications.** The resonance window is drawn about 500× wider than the true natural width so it is visible (SCI-REP-004). "Scattered out of the beam" is said here and again in Beat 5, where "shadow" is introduced; elsewhere "removed" or "absorbed" is shorthand (SCI-RES-001).

## Beat 3 — Temperature becomes line width

> A parcel holds many atoms, each moving its own way: temperature is that random motion.
Count them by their speed along the beam: that census is the shape of the line. Hotter gas, wider line — heat sets its core, but not its faint far wings.

- **Learning objective.** Temperature is particle motion, and the thermal line profile is the census of line-of-sight speeds.
- **User action.** Hold the gas to explore warmer gas (move down while holding for cooler); the temperature ruler and the reading beside the gas report it; touch the census or the line to see which atoms are there; replay how it forms.
- **Visible physical consequence.** Atoms move faster and their line-of-sight arrows lengthen; each atom's arrow travels down to a speed ruler (tail at zero) and leaves a mark at its speed; the marks form a band, stack into the census and settle onto its curve; the curve drops into the parcel's line — wider and shallower when hotter, at fixed amount.
- **Progressive reveal.** 1 · atoms move (temperature is random motion) → 2 · each writes its speed (every atom leaves a mark at its speed along the beam) → 3 · the census (the marks stack up: how many atoms at each speed) → 4 · the line (the census becomes the parcel’s absorption line)
- **Optional equations ("show the physics").**
  - $ b = \sqrt{\dfrac{2kT}{m_{\rm H}}} \approx 12.85\ {\rm km\,s^{-1}}\,\Bigl(\dfrac{T}{10^4\,{\rm K}}\Bigr)^{1/2} $ — the census along the beam is a Gaussian of width b (σ = b/√2) (SCI-THERM-001, SCI-THERM-002)
  - $ \phi_{\rm G}(\Delta v) = \dfrac{1}{\sqrt{\pi}\,b}\,e^{-\Delta v^2/b^2} $ — normalised — heating spreads the same absorption, it does not add any (SCI-THERM-002, SCI-TAU-001)
- **Linked provenance.** SCI-THERM-001 (Maxwellian velocities; one line-of-sight component is Gaussian; verified), SCI-THERM-002 (Doppler parameter and the thermal (Gaussian) profile; verified), SCI-TAU-001 (Optical depth of one absorber; verified), SCI-REP-001 (Representative atoms are a cartoon sample; verified), SCI-CTX-002 (IGM temperature at z ≈ 3; verified)
- **Validation.** VAL-TAU-001: pass
- **Deliberate simplifications.** Thermal motion only; turbulent/unresolved bulk motions within the parcel are ignored (b_turb = 0) unless stated (SCI-THERM-002).
- **Microscope ("why?").** why a Gaussian?
- **Visual transformations.**
  - VT-THERM-WRITE: each atom's speed arrow travels down to one ruler, tail at zero, and its tip leaves a mark at that atom's speed along the beam — representative atoms' line-of-sight velocities, v = g·σ(T) → marks on a speed ruler (a band, darkest where most atoms are) (SCI-THERM-001, SCI-REP-001)
  - VT-THERM-CENSUS: the marks stack into a census and settle onto its curve — marks at each atom's speed → the census of speeds — counts per 2.5 km/s, and the expected count N·Δv·e^(−v²/b²)/(√π b) (SCI-THERM-001, SCI-THERM-002)
  - VT-THERM-LINE: the census curve drops into the parcel's absorption line — the same shape, now in optical depth — the census of line-of-sight speeds (normalised) → the thermal line profile τ(Δv) = τ0(N, b)·e^(−Δv²/b²), at a fixed amount of hydrogen (SCI-THERM-002, SCI-TAU-001)

## Beat 4 — The atom's lifetime leaves faint, far wings

> An excited atom does not stay excited forever, so the colour it absorbs is not perfectly sharp.
This lifetime spread is tiny next to the thermal spread — but far from the centre, it wins. In most forest gas these wings are too faint to see; they show only where the beam crosses a very high column of neutral hydrogen (high N_HI).

- **Learning objective.** The Voigt profile has two physically different pieces — a thermal core and lifetime-driven wings.
- **User action.** Step through the four statements (a chain of reasoning). With "show the physics", a temperature setting changes the core's width; the wings stay.
- **Visible physical consequence.** The survival curve decays in ~1.6 ns; the natural line appears as a hairline; inside the thermal core it is invisible; on a logarithmic scale its wings overtake the Gaussian beyond a few b.
- **Progressive reveal.** 1 · it does not last (the excited state survives ~1.6 ns) → 2 · so not perfectly sharp (a very narrow natural line remains) → 3 · tiny next to motion (thermal motion is well over a thousand times wider) → 4 · far out, it wins (the wings reach farther than the Gaussian)
- **Optional equations ("show the physics").**
  - $ P_{\rm 2p}(t) = e^{-t/t_{\rm 2p}},\qquad t_{\rm 2p} = 1/A_{21} \approx 1.6\ {\rm ns} $ — the chance the atom is still excited (SCI-NAT-001, SCI-ATOM-001)
  - $ \gamma = \dfrac{\Gamma\lambda_0}{4\pi} = 0.0061\ {\rm km\,s^{-1}} $ — natural half-width; Γ = A₂₁ = 6.26×10⁸ s⁻¹; damping parameter a = γ/b (SCI-NAT-001, SCI-ATOM-001)
  - $ H(a,x) \simeq e^{-x^2} + \dfrac{a}{\sqrt{\pi}\,x^2} $ — x = Δv/b; core + wings — the full Voigt function is in the microscope (SCI-VOIGT-001)
- **Linked provenance.** SCI-NAT-001 (Natural broadening from the finite lifetime of 2p; verified), SCI-ATOM-001 (Lyα (H I 1s → 2p) transition data; verified), SCI-VOIGT-001 (The Voigt profile — normalisation, definition and asymptotics; verified), SCI-VOIGT-002 (Numerical Voigt implementation in the app; verified-numeric), SCI-SAT-002 (Where damping wings become visible; verified), SCI-REP-004 (Natural width is magnified wherever it is drawn; verified)
- **Validation.** VAL-VOIGT-001: pass; VAL-TAU-001: pass
- **Deliberate simplifications.** The surface shows only the survival probability; the classical damped-oscillator analogue is in the microscope, labelled as an analogue (SCI-NAT-001). The natural line is magnified (×1200) in the inset and labelled (SCI-REP-004).
- **Microscope ("why?").** why does a short life spread the colour?; how do the two pieces combine?

## Beat 5 — The same colour, stretched

> Hydrogen absorbs at Lyman-alpha in its own frame, scattering that colour out of the beam: a shadow.
Between the gas and us the universe expands: the light stretches, and every shadow written in it stretches too.

- **Learning objective.** Lyα absorption is local and always at 1215.67 Å in the absorber's own frame; the forest is many such shadows, written at different redshifts and stretched on to us, so observed wavelength records where along the way each was written.
- **User action.** Drag the light along its path (or step through, or play, the journey); select a structure in the gas; at the end, zoom into one shadow.
- **Visible physical consequence.** The whole spectral ribbon stretches past a fixed Lyα mark; each structure writes a shadow where the ribbon sits under the mark; earlier shadows move redward as the stretching continues, behind the quasar's own Lyα, which rides the ribbon as a quiet anchor ahead of them all (the close-up keeps a trail of its drift); at our telescope the shadows form the observed forest, the selected one at 1215.67 × (1 + z) Å.
- **Progressive reveal.** 1 · the quasar’s light (a smooth spectrum sets out) → 2 · a structure writes (at 1215.67 Å in its own frame) → 3 · it stretches on (the shadow moves redward with the light) → 4 · the next structure (writes at its own Lyα, on a different part of the light) → 5 · all along the way (the sequence accelerates) → 6 · the forest (at our telescope) → 7 · zoom in (one shadow, read in km/s)
- **Optional equations ("show the physics").**
  - $ \lambda_{\rm here} = \lambda_{\rm emit}\,\dfrac{1+z_{\rm q}}{1+z_{\rm here}} $ — the light's wavelength as measured where it is now; it grows as the light travels (SCI-RED-001, SCI-RED-005)
  - $ \lambda_{\rm here}(z_{\rm abs}) = 1215.67\ \text{Å}\;\Rightarrow\;\lambda_{\rm obs} = 1215.67\ \text{Å}\,(1+z_{\rm abs}) $ — gas at z_abs absorbs what is at Lyα there; we receive that shadow stretched by (1 + z_abs) (SCI-RED-005, SCI-RED-001)
  - $ \lambda_{\rm abs\,frame} = \dfrac{\lambda_{\rm obs}}{1+z_{\rm abs}} $ — the recorded spectrum in the selected structure's rest frame — its own shadow is back at exactly 1215.67 Å (SCI-RED-001)
  - $ \lambda_{\rm q\,frame} = \dfrac{\lambda_{\rm obs}}{1+z_{\rm q}} = 1215.67\,\text{Å}\;\dfrac{1+z_{\rm abs}}{1+z_{\rm q}} < 1215.67\ \text{Å} $ — in the quasar's rest frame every intervening shadow lies blueward of the quasar's own Lyα (SCI-RED-002)
  - $ \ln\lambda_{\rm obs} = \ln\lambda_{\rm here} + \ln(1+z_{\rm here}) $ — on a logarithmic ruler a stretch is a slide (SCI-RED-003)
  - $ \Delta u = c\,\Delta\ln\lambda $ — small slides are the velocities used from Beat 6 on (SCI-RED-003, SCI-MAP-004)
- **Linked provenance.** SCI-RED-001 (Cosmological redshift stretches every wavelength by the same factor; verified), SCI-RED-002 (The quasar's frame — why the forest lies blueward of the quasar's own Lyα; verified), SCI-RED-003 (On a logarithmic ruler a stretch is a slide; small slides are velocities; verified-numeric), SCI-RED-004 (Comoving distance along the light's path (Planck 2018); verified), SCI-RED-005 (The forest is written along the way; verified), SCI-ATOM-001 (Lyα (H I 1s → 2p) transition data; verified), SCI-TAU-001 (Optical depth of one absorber; verified), SCI-FLUX-001 (Transmitted flux (Beer–Lambert); verified), SCI-MAP-001 (Real space → velocity space map; verified), SCI-MAP-004 (Velocity coordinate ↔ observed wavelength; verified), SCI-SIM-TOY-001 (The toy Zel'dovich volume used by the canonical prototype; verified), SCI-REP-007 (The stretching ribbon and the written shadows (Beat 5 representation); verified)
- **Validation.** VAL-RED-001: pass
- **Deliberate simplifications.** The gas along the line of sight is a schematic continuous field (seeded), with three density peaks placed for the narration; its density peaks — the "structures", about thirty along the path — are denser parts of the continuous gas, not separate objects; every bit of it writes at its own Lyα, so peaks write dark shadows and the gas between them faint ones. Shadows are drawn ~60× wider than real forest lines (SCI-REP-007). Only Lyα is drawn; the gas also absorbs Lyβ and higher lines at shorter wavelengths, and the atmosphere hides the far blue (not shown). The surface spectrum is continuum-normalised; the quasar's own Lyα emission appears with "show the physics" (SCI-RED-002). Positions along the path are comoving distances in Planck 2018 cosmology; "measured here" means by an observer at rest in the expanding universe at that point (SCI-RED-004). Each structure's redshift is treated as one number here; Beats 6–7 separate the expansion from the gas's own motion (SCI-MAP-001).
- **Visual transformations.**
  - VT-RED-WRITE: the gas the light is passing writes at a fixed Lyα mark; written shadows ride the ribbon and stretch redward with it — continuous gas along the line of sight (schematic field) → shadows on the stretching ribbon — the forest, written along the way (SCI-RED-005, SCI-RED-001, SCI-REP-007)
  - VT-RED-ANCHOR: the quasar's own Lyα is a quiet mark on the ribbon; it leaves the Lyα mark at the quasar and drifts redward ahead of every shadow — the quasar's Lyα (1215.67 Å in its own frame) → a mark carried by the stretching ribbon, at 1215.67 × (1 + z_q)/(1 + z) where the light is (SCI-RED-002, SCI-RED-001)
  - VT-RED-UNDO: compressing the recorded spectrum undoes the stretch — every shadow and the anchor move together toward short wavelengths — the recorded spectrum in our frame → the same spectrum divided by (1 + z) for a chosen frame (SCI-RED-001, SCI-RED-002, SCI-RED-005)

## Beat 6 — Where does one parcel land?

> One parcel of gas from the 4.4 Mpc/h stretch around the selected shadow. Move it, push it, warm it, or change how much of it is neutral.
Each changes one thing about its ink — its contribution to optical depth — on the spectrum: where it lands (where its ink appears in the spectrum, not where the gas is), how wide, or how much.

- **Learning objective.** Position and bulk velocity set where the contribution lands; temperature and the parcel's size (the Hubble flow across it) set its spread; the neutral amount sets how much — ink is its contribution to optical depth τ.
- **User action.** Move the gas along the beam (its place); push its motion; hold it to explore warmer gas; set the amount of neutral hydrogen with the margin instrument. The rulers and the readings beside the gas report each change; a pencil ghost keeps the state before.
- **Visible physical consequence.** Moving it farther lengthens its recession from the expansion, so it lands redder; pushing it moves where it lands without moving it in space; warmer gas spreads the same ink wider; more neutral hydrogen deepens the ink in place. The ledger place · motion · width · amount marks what changed and what did not; the comparison with the ghost is measured.
- **Optional equations ("show the physics").**
  - $ u = aH(z)\,x_{\rm com} + v_{\rm pec} $ — place (SCI-MAP-001, SCI-MAP-002, SCI-MAP-003)
  - $ b^2 \simeq \dfrac{2kT}{m_{\rm H}} + b_{\rm size}^2,\qquad b_{\rm size} = \sqrt{2}\,aH\,\sigma_x $ — spread: heat and the parcel's size (the Hubble flow across its width σ_x) add in quadrature; here b_size = 23.8 km/s, comparable to the thermal 21.4 km/s (SCI-THERM-002, SCI-REP-003)
  - $ \tau_0 = \dfrac{N_{\rm HI}\,\sigma_v}{\sqrt{\pi}\,b},\qquad \int\tau\,du = N_{\rm HI}\,\sigma_v $ — amount and spread, with the b above (the drawn line's); σ_v = (πe²/m_e c) f λ₀ (SCI-TAU-001, SCI-THERM-002)
- **Linked provenance.** SCI-MAP-001 (Real space → velocity space map; verified), SCI-MAP-002 (Comoving vs physical coordinates and h-units; verified), SCI-MAP-003 (Peculiar-velocity sign convention; verified), SCI-TAU-001 (Optical depth of one absorber; verified), SCI-THERM-002 (Doppler parameter and the thermal (Gaussian) profile; verified), SCI-ION-001 (Photoionisation equilibrium and the neutral-amount control; verified), SCI-ION-002 (How neutral the IGM is; verified), SCI-REP-001 (Representative atoms are a cartoon sample; verified), SCI-REP-003 (Parcels are a teaching decomposition of a continuous sightline; verified), SCI-REP-005 (Ink is optical depth, and the ink rendering performs Beer–Lambert; verified)
- **Validation.** VAL-MAP-001: pass; VAL-TAU-001: pass; VAL-ORTH-001: pass
- **Deliberate simplifications.** The parcel is a teaching Gaussian clump summarising one stretch of the real sightline (SCI-REP-003). Its width along the beam is real space, so the Hubble flow across it spreads its line as much as its temperature does; the margin prints both and the drawn line's own width. Moving the parcel changes only its place; its amount, temperature and own motion travel with it (no density evolution). The "neutral amount" setting changes N_HI directly, holding density, temperature and position fixed; what sets it (ultraviolet light from all galaxies and quasars) is in the microscope (SCI-ION-001). Warming the gas holds N_HI fixed, so that only the width changes; in photoionisation equilibrium the neutral amount would also fall as the gas warms (the recombination rate α_A ∝ T^−0.7, SCI-ION-001). The neutral atoms drawn in the gas are representative (SCI-REP-001), their number proportional to N_HI.
- **Microscope ("why?").** what sets the neutral amount?
- **Visual transformations.**
  - VT-PARCEL-GAS: the parcel drawn as gas carrying representative neutral atoms — their number proportional to N_HI (the gas itself is not enlarged), their random motion to σ(T) — the parcel's state (x, T, N_HI) → a wash at x with dark dots (its neutral atoms) inside it (SCI-REP-001, SCI-REP-003, SCI-THERM-002)
  - VT-PARCEL-MAP: where it lands, as two chained arrows — the recession from the expansion (pencil, from the stretch's near edge) and the parcel's own motion (cinnabar) — place x and own motion v_pec → u = aH·x + v_pec on the velocity axis (SCI-MAP-001, SCI-MAP-002, SCI-MAP-003)
  - VT-PARCEL-BEFORE: the state before a gesture stays as a pencil ghost, with a measured comparison — where it lands, how wide, how much ink — the parcel's optical depth before and after one change → centre shift, FWHM ratio and area ratio printed under the spectrum; the ledger place · motion · width · amount marks what changed (SCI-TAU-001, SCI-MAP-001, SCI-THERM-002)

## Beat 7 — Distance and observed colour are not the same coordinate

> Now the parcel's neighbours: three parcels from the same stretch. Under expansion alone, farther gas recedes faster, so they land in order.
Now push one along the line of sight: its threads (from the gas to where it lands) tilt, and the gas can land out of order — and the gas between the parcels lands too.

- **Learning objective.** The spectrum is organised in observed velocity (wavelength), not simply by real-space distance.
- **User action.** Push a parcel (grab its velocity arrow) and drag its line-of-sight velocity; touch a parcel's gas to select it; switch between expansion alone and the toy's velocities; touch velocity space to see which gas lands there.
- **Visible physical consequence.** Each parcel hangs fine threads from where its gas is to where it lands; they hang straight under pure expansion, tilt with peculiar velocity, fold where the gas converges in velocity, and cross when the order reverses; the flux forms where they land; pencil ghosts mark where expansion alone would put each parcel.
- **Optional equations ("show the physics").**
  - $ u = aH(z)\,x_{\rm com} + v_{\rm pec} $ — x_com comoving; v_pec > 0 means moving away from us (redder); here aH(z)/h = 114.2 km s⁻¹ per Mpc/h (Planck 2018, z = 3) (SCI-MAP-001, SCI-MAP-002, SCI-MAP-003, SCI-MAP-005)
  - $ \lambda_{\rm obs} = \lambda_0\,(1+z_0)\,e^{u/c} $ — the ruler converts velocity to observed wavelength (the stretch of Beat 5, measured in km/s) (SCI-MAP-004)
- **Linked provenance.** SCI-MAP-001 (Real space → velocity space map; verified), SCI-MAP-002 (Comoving vs physical coordinates and h-units; verified), SCI-MAP-003 (Peculiar-velocity sign convention; verified), SCI-MAP-004 (Velocity coordinate ↔ observed wavelength; verified), SCI-MAP-005 (Validity of the constant-H (linear) map; verified-numeric), SCI-REP-003 (Parcels are a teaching decomposition of a continuous sightline; verified)
- **Validation.** VAL-MAP-001: pass; VAL-RED-001: pass
- **Deliberate simplifications.** Three parcels decompose a stretch of the toy sightline; their velocities are the means of the toy's gas, weighted by neutral hydrogen, and the reader may drag them (SCI-REP-003). Velocities are shown relative to the near edge of the stretch.
- **Visual transformations.**
  - VT-MAP-FIBRES: each parcel hangs fine threads from where its gas is to where it lands; straight under expansion alone, tilting, crossing and folding with the gas's own motion — real-space position x of each parcel sub-cell (the cells its τ is computed from) → velocity-space coordinate u = aH(z)·x + v_pec, where its optical depth is placed (SCI-MAP-001, SCI-MAP-003, SCI-REP-003)

## Beat 8 — From parcels back to a continuous sightline

> The three parcels were a teaching summary. Cut the same stretch finer — tens of cells, then the full sampling.
Every cell follows the same rule: map, place its optical depth (its ink), broaden — and the contributions combine.

- **Learning objective.** The toy rules apply cell by cell to a continuous, finely sampled sightline.
- **User action.** Drag the number of cells from 3 up to the full sampling.
- **Visible physical consequence.** The strip goes from three smudges to ruled cells to a continuous band; the optical depth converges to the full calculation (dashed).
- **Optional equations ("show the physics").**
  - $ \tau(u) = \int n_{\rm HI}(x)\,\sigma_v\,\phi\bigl(u - u(x);\,b(x)\bigr)\,dx_{\rm prop} $ — the continuous version of "every cell contributes" (SCI-TAU-002, SCI-SIM-001)
  - valid where each sampling element has one velocity and lines span at least two pixels; outside that domain, particle-based codes differ (up to 0.2 in F for unresolved velocity structure, up to 0.46 for lines narrower than two pixels) — stated, not hidden (SCI-TAU-004, SCI-TAU-005)
- **Linked provenance.** SCI-TAU-002 (Line-of-sight accumulation of optical depth in velocity space; verified), SCI-TAU-004 (One velocity per sampling element (unresolved velocity structure is not represented); verified), SCI-TAU-005 (Discretisation limits — pixel size, pixel averaging and the periodic box; verified), SCI-SIM-001 (The skewer interface (dataset-independent); verified), SCI-SIM-002 (fake_spectra conventions (the later validation target); verified), SCI-SIM-TOY-001 (The toy Zel'dovich volume used by the canonical prototype; verified), SCI-REP-002 (The 3D slab is a teaching volume; only gas on the beam absorbs; verified), SCI-REP-003 (Parcels are a teaching decomposition of a continuous sightline; verified)
- **Validation.** VAL-TOY-001: pass; VAL-CLOSURE-FS: pass (declared domain)
- **Deliberate simplifications.** Real-space cells are the gas re-sampled on a line; particle codes such as fake_spectra deposit each particle's kernel directly in velocity space (VAL-CLOSURE-FS, SCI-SIM-002). One velocity and one temperature per cell. Where several velocities share one cell (unresolved velocity structure), absorption is misplaced; the toy stores one mass-weighted velocity per cell — it discards sub-cell velocity structure by design (SCI-TAU-004). The sum converges only once cells are finer than the narrowest line (aH·Δx ≤ b/2); the coarse slider settings are deliberately under-resolved (SCI-TAU-005).

## Beat 9 — Ink adds

> Every cell has laid its ink in velocity space. Where contributions overlap, they stack.
The ink is optical depth — optical depths add. Dips in the light, the shadows, do not.

- **Learning objective.** Optical depth is the additive quantity.
- **User action.** Play the stacking; toggle "what if dips added instead?".
- **Visible physical consequence.** Transparent contributions stack into the total τ; the wrong rule (adding flux decrements) produces impossible negative light.
- **Optional equations ("show the physics").**
  - $ \tau(u) = \sum_i \tau_i(u) $ — absorbers act independently; their optical depths add (SCI-TAU-002, SCI-TAU-003)
- **Linked provenance.** SCI-TAU-002 (Line-of-sight accumulation of optical depth in velocity space; verified), SCI-TAU-003 (Why optical depths add; verified), SCI-TAU-005 (Discretisation limits — pixel size, pixel averaging and the periodic box; verified), SCI-REP-005 (Ink is optical depth, and the ink rendering performs Beer–Lambert; verified)
- **Validation.** VAL-TAU-001: pass
- **Deliberate simplifications.** The stretch is drawn as 24 cells, coarser than Beat 8's criterion for convergence (half the narrowest line's width); the footer states how far their transmitted flux then differs from the full sampling (SCI-TAU-005). Each cell's optical depth is drawn as one transparent layer of ink; the layers picture the sum, not a physical order along the beam (SCI-REP-005).

## Beat 10 — Light multiplies

> Put the inked ribbon on a light table. Each layer passes a fraction of the light; the fractions multiply.
Where the ink is thick almost nothing gets through: the line saturates, and stops getting deeper. The backlit ribbon is the spectrum of this stretch.

- **Learning objective.** Transmitted flux is F = e^−τ, so transmissions multiply where optical depths add.
- **User action.** Drag the loupe along the ribbon (or along the spectrum) to hold any colour to the light; open "why does a line stop getting deeper?".
- **Visible physical consequence.** The backlit ribbon glows warm where light gets through and stays dark where it does not; the light it lets through also lights the paper around it; the probe lists each layer's transmission and their product; the flux curve is drawn from the light that gets through.
- **Optional equations ("show the physics").**
  - $ F(u) = e^{-\tau(u)},\qquad e^{-\sum_i \tau_i} = \prod_i e^{-\tau_i} $ — the ribbon is rendered by stacking layers of opacity 1 − e^−τᵢ — the picture performs the rule (SCI-FLUX-001, SCI-FLUX-002, SCI-REP-005)
- **Linked provenance.** SCI-FLUX-001 (Transmitted flux (Beer–Lambert); verified), SCI-FLUX-002 (Light multiplies; verified), SCI-REP-005 (Ink is optical depth, and the ink rendering performs Beer–Lambert; verified), SCI-SAT-001 (Saturation and the curve of growth; verified), SCI-SAT-002 (Where damping wings become visible; verified), SCI-CTX-006 (Column-density classes; verified)
- **Validation.** VAL-TAU-001: pass; VAL-REND-001: pass
- **Deliberate simplifications.** The quasar's intrinsic spectrum (continuum) is divided out; F = 1 means "all the expected light arrived".
- **Microscope ("why?").** why does a line stop getting deeper?
- **Visual transformations.**
  - VT-FLUX-LIGHT: the inked ribbon on a light table — each layer passes a fraction of the light; the light that gets through also lights the paper around it — each cell's optical depth τᵢ at each colour → transmitted light e^(−Στᵢ) = Πe^(−τᵢ) (layers of opacity 1 − e^(−τᵢ) over a warm backlight) (SCI-FLUX-001, SCI-FLUX-002, SCI-REP-005)
  - VT-FLUX-LENS: one column of the sheet held to the light, as a lens view — the beam dims at each layer by its fraction e^(−τᵢ) — the optical depths τᵢ of the layers at the inspected colour → the light after each layer, down to the transmitted flux e^(−Στᵢ) (SCI-FLUX-001, SCI-FLUX-002, SCI-REP-005)

## Beat 11 — A forest emerges

> Run the same rules along the toy's full 20 Mpc/h, not just 4.4: the Lyman-alpha forest up close, from 4 863 Å. Dense filaments write its deep lines.
A spectrograph blurs and adds noise to what we record — the gas and its optical depth are untouched.

- **Learning objective.** The forest is the same rules at scale; instrument resolution and noise act only on the final observation.
- **User action.** Zoom out; set the spectrograph's resolution and signal-to-noise (instrument settings — the gas does not change, the measurement does).
- **Visible physical consequence.** The recorded spectrum smooths and gets noisy; the gas strip and τ are visibly unchanged.
- **Optional equations ("show the physics").**
  - $ F_{\rm obs} = F \ast \mathrm{LSF} + n $ — resolution convolves the transmitted flux, not the optical depth (SCI-OBS-001, SCI-OBS-002)
  - $ \sigma_n = 1/(S/N) $ — white noise per detector pixel (SCI-OBS-001, SCI-OBS-002)
  - $ \lambda_{\rm obs} = \lambda_0\,(1+z_0)\,e^{u/c} $ — the observed-wavelength ruler — Beat 5's stretch, read in km/s (SCI-MAP-004)
  - broken line: the data producer's own spectrum (exact Voigt, an independent code path); the browser's differs by at most 6e-04 in F (SCI-SIM-001, SCI-TAU-002)
- **Linked provenance.** SCI-OBS-001 (Instrument resolution acts on the observed flux; verified), SCI-OBS-002 (Noise model and signal-to-noise; verified), SCI-MAP-004 (Velocity coordinate ↔ observed wavelength; verified), SCI-SIM-001 (The skewer interface (dataset-independent); verified), SCI-TAU-002 (Line-of-sight accumulation of optical depth in velocity space; verified), SCI-SIM-TOY-001 (The toy Zel'dovich volume used by the canonical prototype; verified), SCI-CTX-003 (Mean transmitted flux at z ≈ 3; verified), SCI-CTX-004 (H I photoionisation rate at z ≈ 3; verified), SCI-RED-004 (Comoving distance along the light's path (Planck 2018); verified)
- **Validation.** VAL-TOY-001: pass; VAL-TOY-002: pass
- **Deliberate simplifications.** The observer and the quasar are drawn at the ends of the beam for orientation only; the beam is broken at each end because the gaps are not to scale — the toy sample lies ≈ 4384 Mpc/h (comoving) from us, and the quasar farther still (SCI-RED-004). The toy sightline's τ normalisation (Γ_HI) is tuned so the mean transmitted flux is 0.68, as measured at z ≈ 3; the tuned Γ_HI (2.4×10⁻¹² s⁻¹) is ~3× the measured 0.8×10⁻¹², so the toy's absolute ionisation is not a physical claim (SCI-SIM-TOY-001, SCI-CTX-003, SCI-CTX-004). Gaussian line-spread function and white noise of constant σ (SCI-OBS-001, SCI-OBS-002). The student-facing spectrum is the app's own; the generating code's spectrum, an independent check, is an overlay in "show the physics".

## Beat 12 — Who ate this colour?

> The recorded spectrum is all an observer gets. Go backwards — here we can, because we built the gas: point at a colour and light up the gas that absorbed it.
Sometimes one region dominates; sometimes separate places share one colour.

- **Learning objective.** One spectral pixel is not automatically one place in the gas; optical depths from many places add.
- **User action.** Press the spectrum and slide along it — the first time, the colour is traced back slowly; then every colour answers at once (or use the arrow keys); touch the gas to see which colours it takes.
- **Visible physical consequence.** A cinnabar thread rises from the colour into the optical depth, splits by contribution and lands on the gas that absorbed it; those regions develop like ink; then their shares appear and a ledger writes out τ as a sum and F as a product, and the threads fade.
- **Optional equations ("show the physics").**
  - $ \tau(u) = \sum_j \tau_j(u),\qquad F = \prod_j e^{-\tau_j} $ — a colour's optical depth is a sum over all the gas that lands there; the light that gets through is the product (SCI-TAU-003, SCI-FLUX-002)
- **Linked provenance.** SCI-TAU-002 (Line-of-sight accumulation of optical depth in velocity space; verified), SCI-TAU-003 (Why optical depths add; verified), SCI-FLUX-002 (Light multiplies; verified), SCI-MAP-001 (Real space → velocity space map; verified), SCI-RED-004 (Comoving distance along the light's path (Planck 2018); verified)
- **Validation.** VAL-TAU-001: pass; VAL-INV-001: pass
- **Deliberate simplifications.** The observer and the quasar are drawn at the ends of the beam for orientation only; the beam is broken at each end because the gaps are not to scale — the toy sample lies ≈ 4384 Mpc/h (comoving) from us, and the quasar farther still (SCI-RED-004). Shares are computed from the same browser model as the spectrum; regions are grouped by contiguity along the line (the grouping is a display choice).
- **Visual transformations.**
  - VT-INV-TRACE: a chosen colour's thread rises from the spectrum into the optical depth, splits by contribution, and lands on the gas that absorbed it, which develops like ink; only then do the shares appear — one observed colour (a spectral pixel) → the real-space cells whose optical depth makes it, grouped into regions (SCI-TAU-003, SCI-TAU-002, SCI-MAP-001)

## Beat 13 — Same shadow

> Now only the recorded line, as an observer has it — no gas to look up. Three different gases could have made it.
Predict which — then see why the shadow alone cannot tell, and what can.

- **Learning objective.** The spectrum carries physical information, but the inverse problem is not unique; inference must be calibrated, not abandoned.
- **User action.** Choose a gas; reveal; then add a heavier-ion line or Lyman-beta.
- **Visible physical consequence.** All three gases fit the observed line, for two different reasons — the blend (ii) only because of the noise, (iii) because heat and smooth motion widen every hydrogen line alike; a metal line separates heat from bulk motion, and Lyman-beta exposes the hidden column of the blend.
- **Optional equations ("show the physics").**
  - $ b^2 = \dfrac{2kT}{m} + b^2_{\rm bulk} $ — heat broadens light atoms more than heavy ions; bulk motion broadens all alike — every hydrogen line (Lyα, Lyβ, …) sees only the total b, so heat and smooth motion can match in all of them (SCI-DEG-002, SCI-THERM-002)
  - $ \Delta\chi^2 \approx 2.8\ \text{and}\ 0.9\ \ (S/N = 20\ \text{per}\ 2.5\ {\rm km\,s^{-1}}\ \text{pixel}) $ — the blend (ii) is hidden by the noise: at S/N = 50 it shows (Δχ² ≈ 17). (iii) is hidden by what hydrogen records; its small misfit is the hand-tuning, not physics (SCI-DEG-001, SCI-OBS-002)
  - $ F = e^{-\tau} \approx 0\quad(\tau \gg 1) $ — inside the saturated Lyα core almost no light gets through, however the optical depth is split — so the blend (ii) hides there; Lyβ, with a smaller f λ, is not saturated and shows it (SCI-DEG-001, SCI-DEG-002, SCI-SAT-001)
- **Linked provenance.** SCI-DEG-001 (The "same shadow" configurations; verified-numeric), SCI-DEG-002 (What breaks the degeneracy; verified), SCI-OBS-002 (Noise model and signal-to-noise; verified), SCI-THERM-002 (Doppler parameter and the thermal (Gaussian) profile; verified), SCI-SAT-001 (Saturation and the curve of growth; verified), SCI-ATOM-001 (Lyα (H I 1s → 2p) transition data; verified)
- **Validation.** VAL-DEG-001: pass
- **Deliberate simplifications.** The three configurations were tuned by hand to match. Two kinds of "same shadow" are shown — the blend (ii) is hidden only at the stated resolution and S/N (measurement-limited: better data can break it); heat against smooth motion, (i) against (iii), cannot be told apart by any hydrogen line at any S/N (information-limited: hydrogen records only the line-of-sight distribution of velocity and optical depth). The toy's small misfit for (iii) is its hand-tuning (SCI-DEG-001). The three gases are called "clouds" for brevity; each is a denser part of the continuous gas, idealised as one or two smooth Gaussian clumps — not a separate object (SCI-REP-003). The three configurations are a constructed degeneracy example, not typical forest absorbers. Configuration (i) is an idealised compact gas clump — unusually hot (45 000 K, hotter than typical forest gas at z ≈ 3) and only about 7 kpc across (proper), far more compact than typical forest gas — built so that its line matches the other two (SCI-DEG-001).
